seo.title: etcd GUI for {devices}
seo.description: Browse etcd keys by prefix, change values and leases in a grid, and run etcdctl-style get, put, watch and lease commands, with TLS and SSH tunnels.

header.title: etcd GUI
header.lead: Browse keys by prefix, change values and manage leases with etcdctl-style commands.

sections.title: Connect
paragraphs: Enter one host and client port. The peer port has no JSON gateway. There is no database selection or endpoint failover.

Leave Username and Password empty on a cluster without authentication. A user without the root role connects and browses the keys its roles cover, while endpoint status and the user and role commands answer permission denied.

TLS is set by <ui>TLS Mode</ui> in the Advanced fields, not by an SSL section, and starts Disabled. Required (skip verify) encrypts without checking, Verify CA checks the certificate against the CA file you name, and Verify Identity adds the hostname. A client certificate and key add mutual TLS.
Reach a cluster behind a bastion through an SSH tunnel. etcd:// and etcds:// URLs import, and neither switches TLS on by itself.

sections.title: Browse keys and run commands
paragraphs: Set Key Prefix Root, such as /app, to scope a connection to one subtree. The sidebar groups keys by their first path segment under it, and each key is a row with its value, version, mod and create revisions, and lease.

Saving an edit sends commands. A new value or lease puts the key again, a NULL lease removes the lease, and renaming a key puts the new name and deletes the old one. The revision columns belong to etcd, so an edit to one stops the save and names the column.
Run etcdctl-style key, watch, lease, member, endpoint, compaction and access-control commands with command and flag completion. Unsupported commands are rejected before reaching the server.

The etcd driver cannot open a read-only session, so <safeMode>Safe Mode</safeMode> treats every command as a write: at the Alert and Safe Mode levels each one asks first, and Read-Only blocks them all.

sections.title: Leases and the cluster
paragraphs: Manage leases and revision compaction from the editor. Inspect members and endpoint status or health with commands; etcd has no Server Dashboard.

Running auth enable from the editor turns authentication on for the whole cluster. A connection that holds a username and password keeps working; one that holds neither has to be reopened with credentials.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: There is no import. <export>Export</export> keys or a command’s result as {exportFormats}.

faq.question: Why does a lease ID point at a different lease?
faq.answer: Lease IDs take decimal or hex, and hex is recognised by its letters. Prefix an all-digit hex ID with 0x, as in --lease=0x69407712, or it reads as decimal and resolves to another lease.

faq.question: Can I edit binary values?
faq.answer: No. A value that is not valid UTF-8 shows in the grid as its base64, marked as such, and text you type is sent as UTF-8. Write binary values with etcdctl.
